status.main_product: Geospatial analytics platforms and custom spatial intelligence solutions
status.scope_reason: The company develops and sells its own proprietary GIS platforms and software solutions, including Kriti and Smartout, for location analytics and asset intelligence.
status.evidence: According to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs records published on Tofler and ZaubaCorp, the company status is active, and its registered office is in Hyderabad, Telangana.

claims.claim: The company reports its "Kriti" platform serves as a cloud-based enterprise spatial data infrastructure enabling field mapping, asset inventory management, and spatial data logging.
The company reports its "Smartout" platform acts as an integrated geospatial analysis and outage intelligence GIS platform focused on location dynamics and business intelligence.

The company developed a statewide Lake Management and Monitoring System for the government's Mission Kakatiya project in Telangana, which processed 20 years of satellite imagery to map approximately 40,000 surface water bodies across an area of 100,000 square kilometers, according to the official Kaiinos Geospatial website.

The company reports executing a rooftop solar digital twin project for an enterprise client, mapping building attributes such as footprint, height, orientation, and shading for over 65,000 houses across 2 cities using surface models extracted from drone and satellite imagery, as detailed on the Kaiinos Geospatial capabilities platform.

The company partnered with the Telangana government and IIIT-Hyderabad to develop the open-source Lake Management and Monitoring System (LMMS) supporting Mission Kakatiya, utilizing optimized NDWI calculations and rule-based classification algorithms on multispectral satellite data, according to Open Source For You.
The company reports developing "Dharani," a machine learning platform built to automate the extraction of building footprints from satellite imagery, as stated by Industrial Automation India.

The company reports that its GIS platform integrates directly with major enterprise systems of record including SCADA, IoT, ERP (SAP and Oracle), Maximo, ADMS, AMI head-end, and billing systems during its standard deployment workflows.

The company presented its geospatial research work at the National Symposium on "Innovations in Geospatial Technology for Sustainable Development" in Shillong, an industry event organized by the Indian Society of Geomatics and the North-Eastern Space Applications Centre, according to an official corporate announcement.

A multi-stakeholder geospatial project executed in three phases for the development and maintenance of the Telangana Water Resources Information System, in partnership with IIIT Hyderabad, the eGovernance Wing of the Irrigation Department, and the State Data Center under the Government of Telangana, as documented in the Department of Science and Technology's 2022 report.

claims.claim: The deployment of geospatial intelligence and monitoring systems across 21 Indian states, which includes supporting national wildlife surveillance through the M-STrIPES application, as reported by the company.
claims.corrected: The deployment of geospatial intelligence and monitoring systems across 22 Indian states, which includes supporting national wildlife surveillance through the M-STrIPES application, as reported by the company.

claims.claim: According to official regulatory filings retrieved by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) trackers, KAIINOS Geospatial Technologies Private Limited reported annual revenue of ₹1.48 Cr for the financial year ending March 31, 2025, showing a growth of 51% compared to the previous year.
In the same financial year filings (FY 2025), the company recorded an EBITDA of ₹16.48 Lakh (an EBITDA margin of 11.1%) and a net profit of ₹6.79 Lakh.
claims.note: EBITDA and EBITDA margin details could not be verified in the retrieved financial reporting snippets.

claims.claim: A collaborative partnership with the Telangana government and IIIT-Hyderabad to develop an open-source Lake Management and Monitoring System (LMMS) utilizing satellite data and location-based applications, as reported by Open Source For You.
The company reports catering to over 35,000 users across India, executing more than 40 enterprise deployments, and mapping over 300,000 square kilometers across 27 states and regions.
